text_blocks.snippet: According to the DSM-5 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, 5th Edition), a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) requires the presence of five or more symptoms of depression, with at least one of them being either a depressed mood or a loss of interest or pleasure (anhedonia), lasting for at least two weeks. These symptoms must also represent a change from previous functioning and cause significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of life.
